database_configuration.connection_pooling: Explicit context instantiation per transactional module execution via `databases.py` — one `connection()` call, `conn.close()` in a `finally` block, per module function; no persistent pool
database_configuration.driver_interface: pymssql (FreeTDS-based) — `connection()` reads LOCAL_DB_SERVER / LOCAL_DB_NAME / LOCAL_DB_USER / LOCAL_DB_PASSWORD from env
database_configuration.data_format_strategy: Heavy usage of T-SQL `FOR JSON PATH` options to return natively compressed serialization streams directly to FastAPI responses

connection_resilience.issue: FreeTDS has a known `tds_dataout_stream_write` assertion crash when a single `EXEC sp @pjsonfile = %s` call sends a large NVARCHAR(MAX) parameter (large JSON payloads — e.g. multi-image blob-URL clientFaceRecognitions writes) through pymssql's normal parameterized-query path.
connection_resilience.fix: `databases.py` wraps the driver cursor in a `SafeCursor` class that intercepts single-param `EXEC ... @pjsonfile = %s` calls and rewrites them server-side as `DECLARE @_json NVARCHAR(MAX); SET @_json = N'...'; EXEC ... @_json` before sending, avoiding the crash path entirely. `DatabaseConnection` wraps `pymssql.Connection.cursor()` to always hand back a `SafeCursor`.
connection_resilience.scope: Applied once, centrally, in `databases.py` — every module's existing `EXEC [dbo].[sp_x] @pjsonfile = %s` call pattern is automatically safe; no per-module changes were needed.
